actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a collection of robot models tailored to robosuite
The card's first model is the MJCF document whose root element is '<mujoco model="aloha">'
The Aloha wrapper loads the same file through robosuite_model_path_completion("robots/aloha/robot.xml")
The Aloha wrapper describes the robot as bimanual with two arms and lists the arms right and left
The right arm is a chain of six hinge joints named right/waist, right/shoulder, right/elbow, right/forearm_roll, right/wrist_angle and right/wrist_rotate
The left arm is the matching chain of six hinge joints named left/waist, left/shoulder, left/elbow, left/forearm_roll, left/wrist_angle and left/wrist_rotate

The actuator section declares twelve motor actuators, one per joint; the control ranges are waist -5 to 5, shoulder -50 to 50, elbow -50 to 50, forearm_roll -5 to 5, wrist_angle -1 to 1 and wrist_rotate -1 to 1, repeated for the left arm
The model sets no option timestep: the compiler and option elements are inside an XML comment at lines 2-4, so no <option timestep> element is active
The finger default classes, with a slide joint range and a position ctrlrange, are inside an XML comment at lines 34-43, so those finger defaults are not active in this model
The Aloha wrapper attaches the AlohaGripper to the right and left arms by default; the gripper is not part of robot.xml
The model declares its six visual meshes as STL files with a 0.001 scale under meshes/

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the served robot.xml for the 12 joints, the 12 actuator ctrlranges and the time step, then moves each actuated joint toward its control value; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, equality or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact: the six STL meshes of the model are not read, and the two contact exclusions of the model are not applied

the served robot.xml is the bare two-arm model; the AlohaGripper that the robosuite wrapper attaches to each arm (aloha_robot.py:26-35) is not part of this MJCF, so no finger joint or gripper actuator is served
the model sets no option timestep; the stand-in uses a placeholder library default as the step (fake.py), and the bridge publishes that stand-in value from the stand-in
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the two wrist cameras of the model are not exposed, and only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is published
no physical Aloha robot is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the integration state stays readable
